text:
jordan: Heads-up: ran into an odd panicking iterator in the Go sample app when token refresh + client cancel happen concurrently. Minimal repro below — it's pretty flaky but happens reliably with forced refresh.

nina: Can you drop the snippet + the stack trace?

jordan: Paste:
```go
// sample/main.go (excerpt)
ctx := context.Background()                 // sample uses Background atm
c := redwood.NewClient(ctx, redwood.Opts{Model: "redwood-small"})
iter := c.Generator().Stream("prompt")
for iter.Next() {
    fmt.Print(iter.Value().Text)
    // client cancels from signal handler elsewhere
}
if err := iter.Err(); err != nil {
    log.Println("stream error:", err)
}
```
stack: 
```
panic: send on closed channel
goroutine 78 [running]:
redwood/gen.(*streamer).handlePush(0xc000...)
...
```

jordan: Repro steps: run sample with TTL=2s token and a background goroutine that calls client.Close() after ~1s while iterating. Sometimes we get duplicate Close errors, sometimes panic.

harry: Two likely issues: 1) sample uses context.Background() instead of request ctx so lifecycle is fuzzy; 2) token refresh swaps transport/token source mid-stream without syncing with active stream goroutines.

harry: Fix ideas: make the stream iterator own the transport lifecycle (iterator.Close() does teardown). Also ensure token refresh uses singleflight or a mutex so only one goroutine mutates shared transport state.

nina: From a DX POV, users copy the sample verbatim. We should change sample to provide a request-scoped example: NewGenerator(req.Context(), ...) and show iterator.Close in the loop. Add a short note explaining why Background is usually wrong for streaming.

jordan: Agreed. I sketched a small change:
```go
// handler style
func Serve(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
  gen := redwood.NewGenerator(r.Context(), redwood.Opts{})
  it := gen.Stream("hi")
  defer it.Close() // clearly owned by the handler
  for it.Next() {
    w.Write([]byte(it.Value().Text))
  }
}
```

harry: API change discussion: do we want NewGenerator(...) to return a generator tied to that ctx, or add a NewRequestGenerator helper? Either is fine but we should avoid breaking changes. Maybe add a new Streamer iterator type that implements Close() error and keep old API as compatibility shim.

nina: Also add an integration test: spawn N goroutines consuming same type of stream while forcing token refresh and client cancellation. Run -race and assert no panics and deterministic Err() values. Include TTL toggle script for reproducibility.

devparity-bot: Note: Please file a parity-ticket if we change surface. See PARITY-58 checklist.

jordan: Filed INF-3249: "go sample: stream lifecycle races with auth refresh" and attached repro + tiny TTL toggle script.

ops-bot: created issue INF-3249 and linked to CI job that runs the repro with -race nightly.

nina: For docs: add a short "Common streaming pitfalls" entry in the Go quickstart: include Background caveat, token-refresh guidance (singleflight or dedicated token source per connection), and sample that uses request ctx. People keep copying the sample into services and hit this in production.

harry: One more thought: circuit-breaker the token refresh path so a bad token server doesn't cause aggressive reconnects mid-stream. Also log a clear event when we rotate transport due to auth so customers can trace failures.

jordan: I'll send a small PR updating the sample, add the integration test and TTL script, and prototype the iterator-ownership change as a follow-up PR behind a compatibility flag. Will include a docs patch.

nina: Please @dev-parity when the PR is up. Thanks for catching this early. :rocket:
